construct.diagnosis_or_process: Primary hyperoxaluria type 2 due to GRHPR deficiency
construct.mechanism: GRHPR deficiency impairs glyoxylate reduction and hydroxypyruvate metabolism, increasing endogenous oxalate production. PH2 causes recurrent calcium-oxalate stones/nephrocalcinosis and characteristically increased urinary L-glycerate; biallelic GRHPR variants establish the diagnosis.
construct.primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

second_answer_attack.resolution: PH1 and PH2 both cause childhood calcium-oxalate stones, but increased urinary L-glycerate is the classic biochemical discriminator for GRHPR/PH2; PH1 more often shows increased glycolate and is caused by AGXT.
